'''John Robert Taylor''' is a British-born [[emeritus professor]] of [[physics]] at the [[University of Colorado, Boulder]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Core Faculty in the Department of Physics | publisher = [[University of Colorado, Boulder]] | url = http://www.colorado.edu/physics/Web/directory/faculty/index.html | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20100528024546/http://www.colorado.edu/physics/Web/directory/faculty/index.html | archivedate = 2010-05-28 }}</ref>

He received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in [[mathematics]] at [[Cambridge University]], and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1963 with thesis advisor [[Geoffrey Chew]].<ref>{{cite web | publisher = [[University of Colorado, Boulder]] | title = John R. Taylor C.V. | url = http://www.colorado.edu/UCB/AcademicAffairs/ArtsSciences/physics/TZD/TaylorZafDubVitae/TaylorVita.txt | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20121013143013/http://www.colorado.edu/UCB/AcademicAffairs/ArtsSciences/physics/TZD/TaylorZafDubVitae/TaylorVita.txt | archivedate = 2012-10-13 }}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=57786|title=John Robert Taylor}}</ref> Taylor has written several college-level physics textbooks. His bestselling book is ''An Introduction to Error Analysis'',<ref>{{cite book | title = An Introduction to Error Analysis: The Study of Uncertainties in Physical Measurements  | author = John R. Taylor | year = 1996 | publisher = University Science Books | isbn = 978-0-935702-75-0}}</ref> which has been translated into nine languages. His intermediate-level undergraduate textbook, ''Classical Mechanics'', was well-reviewed.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Taylor | first1=John R. | last2=Cook | first2=Gayle | title=Post-Use Review: Classical Mechanics | journal=American Journal of Physics | publisher=American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT) | volume=72 | issue=4 | year=2004 | issn=0002-9505 | doi=10.1119/1.1634968 | pages=559| bibcode=2004AmJPh..72..559T }}</ref>

==Awards==
Taylor was designated a [[Presidential Teaching Scholar]]  in 1991.<ref>{{cite web | publisher = [[University of Colorado, Boulder]] | title = President's Teaching Scholars Program | url = http://www.colorado.edu/ptsp/about/administration.html | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20100530105931/http://www.colorado.edu/ptsp/about/administration.html | archivedate = 2010-05-30 }}</ref> He has also received an [[Emmy Award]] for his television series ''Physics 4 Fun'' (1988–1990).<ref>{{cite press release | title = John Taylor Named Hazel Barnes Prize Winner | publisher = [[University of Colorado, Boulder]] | url = http://www.colorado.edu/chancellor/awards/taylor.html | date = 1999-05-12 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20101215010159/http://colorado.edu/chancellor/awards/taylor.html | archivedate = 2010-12-15 }}</ref>
